Fixture: 16_modular_gray_511x8_multisection_lossless.jxl
511x8 grayscale, mathematically lossless -- tiny multi-section smoke fixture

Purpose
-------
A cheap regression companion to 14/15 (see those sidecars for the full
multi-section rationale). 14/15 are the fixtures that satisfy AGENTS.md
section 6's "any path that can see more than one group gets a >=256x256
fixture" rule; this one does NOT (511x8 is nowhere near 256 tall) and is not
meant to. Its only job is to exercise the same TOC/group-copy code path
(F.3, G.2.3, G.4.2) at a small fraction of the byte count, for a fast test
that still fails loudly if that path regresses.

511x8 was found by probing cjxl empirically (permitted -- running the binary
as a black box, never reading its source, per AGENTS.md section 2): images
narrower than the 512px threshold that makes 12_modular_gray_300x200 pick
`group_dim = 512` can still get `group_dim = 256` from this cjxl build when
one dimension is very small (8px here). This is a black-box behavioural
observation about one cjxl build, not a documented or guaranteed encoder
rule -- if a future oracle rebuild changes it and this fixture stops being
multi-section, tests/e2e_multisection.rs's `num_sections > 1` assertion
catches that (see the note on 14's sidecar making the same point). 511 (not
512) was chosen deliberately: at 512 wide this build already picks
`group_dim = 256` too in some configurations, but 511 keeps the image
strictly under the "exceeds 512" lever that 14/15 use, so this fixture
demonstrates the second, independent behaviour rather than duplicating it.

Provenance
----------
  Encoder:      cjxl v0.13.0 196a43d9 [_AVX2_,SSE4,SSE2] {GNU 15.2.0}
  libjxl rev:   196a43d996aa6ed33ebf98812a7c6d43b2b6d01b (v0.12-snapshot-2-g196a43d9)
  cjxl flags:   -d 0 -e 7
  Built by:     tools/setup-oracles.sh (flags recorded in
                tools/oracle-bin/PINNED_REVISIONS.txt)
  Regenerate:   tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh
                That script IS the recipe; it rewrites the source and re-encodes.

  Source image: tests/fixtures/generated/src_gray_511x8.pgm  (4101 bytes)
                sha256 8504dad3065b4390cc0464fd5f18e35b870b17efbdcbdb65fb17af397d7dfd27
                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was
                used, converted, or consulted. 511x8 8-bit grayscale (PGM
                P5):
                  v(x, y) = (x + y) * 255 / 517     diagonal ramp, 0..255
                Same diagonal-ramp family as 07/08/12/14.

  Fixture:      121 bytes
                sha256 f5584ec393d86c8d90961986de87c740e17059aca573367ad751564b59621ffc

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PGM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run
of tools/make-modular-fixtures.sh). Classified by `jpxl info` (jpxl-cli) as
a recognized "naked codestream", 121 bytes.

Independently, this crate's own `FrameGeometry::from_header` + `read_toc`
report `group_dim = 256`, `num_groups = 2` (a 2x1 grid: one full 256-wide
group and one 255-wide partial right-edge group, both 8 tall), `num_sections
= 5` (2 header sections + 1 LF group + 2 pass groups) for this fixture --
see tests/e2e_multisection.rs.

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
Multi-section tiling with a partial right-edge group, at minimal size. cjxl
printed nothing transform-specific at encode time; jxlinfo is not built in
this checkout; djxl -v / -v -v print no per-feature detail for this stream.
See 07_modular_gray_8x8_lossless.jxl.txt for the general caveat on
feature-introspection limits.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
